### aws-auto-scaling-aas-cooldown-larger-scale-out

**Claim.** Application Auto Scaling keeps evaluating metrics during a cooldown period, and if a larger scale-out is needed during the cooldown the policy scales out immediately.

**Write it as.** `continues to evaluate metrics during the cooldown` · `the scaling policy scales out immediately`

**Scope.** per Application Auto Scaling scalable target.

> "A cooldown period between scaling activities lets the resource stabilize before another scaling activity starts. Application Auto Scaling continues to evaluate metrics during the cooldown period. When the cooldown period ends, the scaling policy initiates another scaling activity if needed. While a cooldown period is in effect, if a larger scale out is necessary based on the current metric value, the scaling policy scales out immediately."
> — [Application Auto Scaling concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/getting-started.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-13.

### aws-auto-scaling-aas-out-of-band-corrected

**Claim.** Capacity changed out of band outside a scalable target's minimum-maximum range is brought back into that range the next time a scaling policy is invoked or RegisterScalableTarget is called.

**Write it as.** `out-of-band changes` · `updated to comply with the set minimum`

**Scope.** per Application Auto Scaling scalable target.

> "You can make out-of-band changes directly to the underlying resource that are outside of this range, which Application Auto Scaling doesn't know about. However, anytime a scaling policy is invoked or the `RegisterScalableTarget` API is called, Application Auto Scaling retrieves the current capacity and compares it to the minimum and maximum capacity. If it falls outside of the minimum-maximum range, then the capacity is updated to comply with the set minimum and maximum."
> — [Application Auto Scaling concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/getting-started.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-13.
